# netactuate_router_vrf_interface_wireguard_peer (Resource)

Beta. The cloud router family is in beta: behaviour and schema may change. Manages a WireGuard peer on a cloud router VRF interface.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netactuate_router_vrf_interface_wireguard_peer" "example" {
  allowed_ips {
    network = "192.0.2.0/24"
  }
  interface_id = 12345
  router_id    = 12345
  vrf_id       = 12345
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `allowed_ips` (Block List, Min: 1) The list of IP networks allowed to traverse the tunnel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--allowed_ips))
- `interface_id` (Number) The ID of the wireguard interface.
- `router_id` (Number) The ID of the cloud router.
- `vrf_id` (Number) The ID of the VRF.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description of the wireguard interface.
- `name` (String) The name of the wireguard interface.
- `pre_shared_key` (String, Sensitive) An optional pre-shared key for additional security.
- `public_key` (String, Sensitive) The base64 public key for the wireguard peer. If not provided, a key pair will be generated.
- `remote` (String) The remote address of the wireguard interface.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The base64 private key for the wireguard peer (only available if generated by the system).
- `wireguard_peer_id` (Number) The ID of the wireguard peer.

<a id="nestedblock--allowed_ips"></a>
### Nested Schema for `allowed_ips`

Required:

- `network` (String) An individual allowed network in CIDR notation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import netactuate_router_vrf_interface_wireguard_peer.example 12345
```
